section: Leaving Germany: exit tax on company shares (Wegzugsteuer)
wording: Figures are for tax year 2026. This Guide covers the German side only: the exit tax on company shares under § 6 of the Foreign Tax Act (Außensteuergesetz, AStG) and the extended limited tax liability under § 2 AStG that can follow a move to a low-tax country. It reads the current consolidated text on gesetze-im-internet.de, which applies to income tax from the 2022 assessment year onwards (§ 21(1) AStG). Departures before 1 January 2022 follow the old wording of § 6 (§ 21(3) AStG) and are out of scope. This is a working paper for review, not a filed return.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

section: Leaving Germany: exit tax on company shares (Wegzugsteuer)
wording: The rules of the arrival country must be checked separately. For a move to the United Arab Emirates, see `ae-tax-residency`. For a move to Switzerland, use `germany-to-switzerland-cross-border-tax`, which covers the Swiss side and the German rules for commuters and weekly stayers; this Guide stops at its edge. For a German sale of shares while still resident, see `de-capital-gains`. For a comparison of exit taxes in several countries, see `exit-taxes-when-a-family-moves`. For general German tax planning, see `germany-tax-optimization`.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 1. Test the shares. § 6 AStG refers to shares within § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG. Test the holder's own direct or indirect minimum participation within the last five years, and the recent free-acquisition/predecessor exception below. This uses the combined-source reading of § 6(1) AStG with § 17(1) sentence 4 EStG described under "Which shares". The test concerns the company's capital, so shares in a German GmbH and in a foreign company both count. See [§ 17 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__17.html).
disposition: Bounded source/condition successor

wording: 2. Test the person. § 6 applies only to a natural person who was fully taxable in Germany (unbeschränkt steuerpflichtig under § 1(1) EStG) for at least seven years in total within the twelve years before the triggering event. For shares received free of charge (gift or inheritance), the periods of the giver count too, and overlapping periods count once. See [§ 6(2) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 3. Identify the trigger and its date. There are three triggers in § 6(1) AStG: the end of full tax liability because the person gives up the German residence or habitual abode (taxed at the moment liability ends); a free transfer of the shares to a person who is not fully taxable in Germany (taxed at the moment of transfer); and any other exclusion or restriction of Germany's right to tax the gain on the shares (taxed immediately before that happens). See [§ 6(1) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 4. Compute the deemed gain. The trigger counts as a sale of the shares at their fair market value (gemeiner Wert). The gain is that value less sale costs less acquisition cost (§ 17(2) EStG), and it is business income (§ 17(1) EStG). Apply the partial-income method: the exempt share in the § 3 table below (§ 3 no. 40 letter c EStG); sale costs and the acquisition cost just used to compute the gain are themselves deductible only at the share in the § 3c table below, because § 3c(2) EStG's second half-sentence extends the same limit to acquisition cost taken into account in determining income. Then apply the § 17(3) allowance, which is scaled to the share sold and shrinks as the gain grows. See [§ 17 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__17.html), [§ 3 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3.html) and [§ 3c EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3c.html).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 5. Decide on instalments. On application, the tax on the deemed gain can be paid in seven equal yearly instalments, without interest, normally only against security. See [§ 6(4) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 6. If the move may be temporary, test the return rule. The tax lapses if the person becomes fully taxable again within seven years and the conditions in "Coming back" below are met. See [§ 6(3) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 7. Diary the reporting duties after leaving: an electronic notice within one month of any event that makes the remaining tax due, and a yearly confirmation of address and ownership by 31 July. See [§ 6(5) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 8. Test the extended limited tax liability for the ten years after the year of departure: a German citizen moving to a low-tax country (or to no country) while keeping substantial economic interests in Germany. See [§ 2 AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__2.html).

wording: **Who.** Only natural persons. The seven-year test counts years of full tax liability under § 1(1) EStG, in total, not in a row. Where the shares were received free of charge, the full tax liability of the giver (and of each earlier giver in a chain of free transfers) is added, and years in which both were fully taxable count only once. A person whose earlier exit tax lapsed because they came back is treated as covered without the seven-year test, and so is their direct or indirect successor (§ 6(2) sentence 4 AStG).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: **Which shares.** Shares within § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG. § 17(1) sentence 3 defines them: shares (Aktien), GmbH shares, profit participation rights (Genussscheine) and similar participations, rights to acquire such shares, and shares in a company that opted to be taxed as a corporation under § 1a KStG. Shares in a cooperative also count (§ 17(7) EStG). § 6(1) AStG applies subject to the rules of the Income Tax Act, the Corporation Tax Act and the Reorganisation Tax Act, so shares held as business assets need a separate check (see "When to refuse or refer").

section: How the deemed gain is taxed
wording: The deemed sale is a sale under § 17(1) EStG, and § 17(1) sentence 1 makes that gain income from business (Einkünfte aus Gewerbebetrieb). The gain is the amount by which the sale price, after sale costs, exceeds the acquisition cost (§ 17(2) sentence 1 EStG); for § 6 AStG the sale price is the fair market value. Acquisition cost includes incidental costs and later costs such as open or hidden capital contributions (§ 17(2a) EStG). Under § 3c(2) EStG, this acquisition cost is itself deductible only at the share in the § 3c table below, not in full: its second half-sentence reaches "die Anschaffungs- oder Herstellungskosten ... mindernd zu berücksichtigen sind", not only sale costs.

section: How the deemed gain is taxed
wording: The allowance in the § 17 table above is not a flat amount. It is the part of that amount that matches the share of the company being taxed, and it falls by the excess of the gain over the matching part of the taper amount, so for a large holding it is usually gone. Tax rates and the solidarity surcharge are not repeated here; see `de-einkommensteuer-freelancer` for the tariff.

wording: If the end of full tax liability rests on an absence that is only temporary, and the person becomes fully taxable in Germany again within seven years of leaving, the exit tax lapses. It lapses only to the extent that all three of these hold:
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: 2. there were no profit distributions or returns of capital whose total fair market value is more than one quarter of the value at exit; and
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: A transfer on death to a natural person does not break condition 1, if that person (or a later heir by death) meets the conditions. The tax office that was competent when the person left (§ 19 AO) may extend the seven years, on application, by at most five years in total, if the intention to return still exists. The same rules apply where the trigger was a restriction of Germany's taxing right caused by a temporary absence, and where shares were given to a natural person who becomes fully taxable in Germany within seven years of the gift.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: **Payment in return cases.** Where a return is planned, the tax is deferred for the period the tax office grants. On application, no instalments are collected. Beyond the five events above, the tax falls due within one month after an event that means the tax can no longer lapse, or after the person tells the tax office they no longer intend to return. If the tax does not lapse and the person chose not to pay instalments, interest is charged for the deferral period under § 234 AO (§ 6(4) last sentences AStG).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

section: R11–17 new ordinary condition / computed separator / actual source read
wording: **Recent free acquisition: combined-source interpretation.** Read § 6(1) AStG's reference to § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG together with § 17(1) sentence 4, which expressly applies sentence 1 to the following predecessor case. If the relevant share was acquired free of charge within the five years before the deemed disposal, a holder who did not personally meet the 1% test must still be tested where the predecessor, or an earlier predecessor in a chain of free transfers, met that participation test within the relevant five-year period under sentence 1. Record the acquisition and each relevant transfer date, direct/indirect holdings and the predecessor's qualifying holding dates. A recent gift or inheritance of a 0.5% share therefore does not fail solely because the current holder never reached 1%, if the qualifying predecessor test is met. This is a separate shareholding rule from the residence-period aggregation in § 6(2) AStG; all other person, trigger and tax-chain conditions still apply.
